summary: QuantaPay POC benchmark: suspected p95 latency regression during agreed measurement window (Dedicated us-east)
related_confluence_pages: Support Runbook: Dedicated Latency Regression Triage
Metrics Validation Worksheet (Go-to-market drive): QuantaPay tab
description:
Issue summary
- During the QuantaPay POC benchmarking window, Console + customer-side measurement show an increase in p95 end-to-end latency for chat completions on qp-prod-chat.
- Customer flagged the change as a regression vs the prior baseline run and asked us to pause “final metrics” collection until we can explain and/or mitigate.

Impact
- Benchmark numbers used for POC acceptance and (conditional) case study metrics are not currently trustworthy.
- No confirmed production outage, but benchmark run is blocked pending root cause and a stable measurement window.

Customer context
- QuantaPay is running a traffic replay benchmark (recorded production-like prompts) against their Dedicated pool.
- Success criteria (per POC scoping): stable p95 latency at agreed concurrency + low error rate; any metrics to be published must match a reproducible methodology.

Environment
- Deployment: Redwood Dedicated (QuantaPay) / us-east
- Cluster: qp-dedicated-use1
- Route: /v1/chat/completions (streaming=true for most runs)
- Auth: org qp_prod, project qp_poc_benchmark
- Observability: Redwood Console dashboards + customer’s k6 runner metrics

What changed / suspected triggers
- Potential runtime/scheduler change observed in the cluster around 2025-06-03 evening (node replacement + new serving container digest).
- Batch scheduler config may have been auto-tuned after traffic shape changed (longer prompts in replay set) leading to queueing at higher concurrency.

Baseline vs observed (customer reported)
- Baseline window (agreed): 2025-05-29 10:00–12:00 ET
  - p50: ~210–240 ms
  - p95: ~390–430 ms
  - errors: <0.2%
- Regression window: 2025-06-04 09:00–11:00 ET
  - p50: ~240–280 ms (small change)
  - p95: ~650–820 ms (large change)
  - errors: still low (<0.5%), but intermittent first-token delay spikes noted on streaming

Steps to reproduce (internal)
1) Use the QuantaPay replay harness (k6) with concurrency=64, prompt mix “qp_replay_set_v3”.
2) Hit qp-prod-chat with streaming enabled.
3) Observe p95 and first-token delay (FTD) over a 30-min steady-state period.

Expected result
- p95 should remain within baseline band (+/- ~10–15%) given no intentional changes to model/route configuration.

Actual result
- p95 increases by ~60–100% with visible queueing bursts (sawtooth) consistent with scheduler/batching interaction or GPU saturation.

Evidence / logs (snippets)
- API gateway timing (sample requests during regression window):
  - 2025-06-04T13:22:41Z request_id=req_01HY9Q4Z7W9WQJ2H8P9C7J2A2M route=qp-prod-chat status=200 total_ms=1184 ttfb_ms=612 tokens_out=182 prompt_tokens=1480 model=llama-3.1-70b-instruct stream=true
  - 2025-06-04T13:23:05Z request_id=req_01HY9Q53S0Z8H9M6Q6Z5J9QK2A route=qp-prod-chat status=200 total_ms=1049 ttfb_ms=544 tokens_out=166 prompt_tokens=1522 model=llama-3.1-70b-instruct stream=true
  - 2025-06-04T13:24:12Z request_id=req_01HY9Q6K0FQ3J3XJ1M1W0Z2H4P route=qp-prod-chat status=200 total_ms=1422 ttfb_ms=701 tokens_out=204 prompt_tokens=2011 model=llama-3.1-70b-instruct stream=true

- Serving runtime trace (selected):
  - trace_id=trc_7f2c3e9 span=scheduler.queue_wait_ms value=410 node=qp-use1-gpu-12 batcher=continuous
  - trace_id=trc_7f2c3e9 span=gpu.decode_ms value=512 seq_out=190 kv_cache_hit=false
  - trace_id=trc_a19b22d span=scheduler.queue_wait_ms value=533 node=qp-use1-gpu-07 batcher=continuous

- No obvious throttling:
  - 429 rate limit: not observed in sample set
  - 5xx: sporadic 502 (<0.1%), likely client disconnects on streaming retries

Initial hypotheses
1) Scheduler/batching config: higher max_batch_tokens causing queue wait spikes under the replay’s long-prompt distribution.
2) Node image / driver change: slight perf degradation on a subset of GPUs causing tail latency.
3) KV cache behavior: reduced cache reuse (kv_cache_hit=false) due to prompt diversity, increasing tail.
4) Noisy neighbor: unlikely (dedicated), but check GPU utilization and kernel launch stalls.

Customer-facing ask
- Customer wants a clear statement of (a) root cause or (b) mitigation + a fresh, mutually agreed measurement window for final results.

Next actions (this ticket)
- Confirm whether a runtime container digest or scheduler config changed between baseline and regression windows.
- Identify if regression is node-correlated (subset of GPU hosts) vs systemic.
- Propose mitigation (config pin / rollback / tune) and schedule a re-run with QuantaPay.

Owners
- Primary: Simran Kaur (Solutions Architect)
- Support: Logan Wright (telemetry + metrics validation)
- Sales/POC coordination: Priyom Das (AE)

Notes for case study
- Do not use any QuantaPay performance numbers externally until we have (1) a validated stable window and (2) documented measurement methodology + caveats approved by customer.
comments: 2025-06-04 10:18 ET — Logan Wright (Reporter): QuantaPay flagged p95 regression on qp-prod-chat during today’s benchmark window. Console corroborates (p95 ~780ms vs ~420ms last week). Creating SUP-2444 to track RCA + mitigation before we lock case study metrics. Priyom + Simran looped in.

2025-06-04 10:32 ET — Simran Kaur (Assignee): Acknowledged. Pulling cluster change history + comparing baseline window vs current. First suspicion: scheduler/batcher settings changed with the new node rotation on 6/3. Will update with diffs and propose a rollback/tuning option within 24h.

2025-06-04 11:05 ET — Priyom Das (AE): Customer is okay to pause today’s run, but they want a written explanation and a new measurement window by Friday. They also asked if we can pin to “known-good” settings for the remainder of POC.

2025-06-04 12:14 ET — Logan Wright: Quick check: error rate stayed low; the issue is mostly tail + first-token delay. Queue_wait_ms spikes align with p95 spikes. Seeing kv_cache_hit=false more often in traces for the replay set. This might be expected, but tail jump still seems too large vs baseline with similar replay mix.

2025-06-04 13:02 ET — Simran Kaur: Found a likely change: qp-dedicated-use1 rolled to serving container digest sha256:8c1e… late 6/3 as part of standard image refresh. Also seeing batcher config ‘max_batch_tokens’ increased from 8192 -> 12288 (auto-tune) on qp-prod-chat. Hypothesis: larger batches improve avg but worsen tail under long prompts due to queueing. Proposing we pin max_batch_tokens back to 8192 and re-run.
2025-06-04 13:20 ET — Logan Wright: +1. Please also check if the regression is isolated to certain nodes. I can run a per-node p95 breakdown if you can confirm node labels for qp-prod-chat pods.

2025-06-04 14:06 ET — Simran Kaur: Per-node check: qp-use1-gpu-07 and qp-use1-gpu-12 show the biggest queue_wait spikes. Not sure if hardware variance or just load skew. I’m requesting SRE to drain those nodes post-change so we can see if tail tightens.

2025-06-05 09:11 ET — Logan Wright: Applied config pin (max_batch_tokens=8192) in qp-prod-chat at 08:40 ET. Early smoke at concurrency=32 shows p95 back to ~460–510ms. Need a full 60-min run at concurrency=64 to confirm.

2025-06-05 10:27 ET — Simran Kaur: SRE drained qp-use1-gpu-07; qp-use1-gpu-12 still in service. Re-run in progress. If p95 stabilizes, we’ll keep pinned settings for the rest of POC and note that auto-tune can be disabled for benchmark windows.

2025-06-06 15:44 ET — Priyom Das: Customer asked whether the ‘regression’ was caused by us changing something mid-POC. I told them we did an image refresh + auto-tune adjustment, and we’ve now pinned settings for benchmarking. They want that summarized in email plus a clear measurement plan for final metrics.

2025-06-07 11:08 ET — Logan Wright: Full rerun results (qp_replay_set_v3, concurrency=64, 60-min steady state): p50 ~235ms, p95 ~455ms, errors 0.18%. FTD p95 improved materially (was ~600–700ms during regression; now ~320–380ms). Suggest we treat 6/4 window as invalid due to config drift and use 6/7 as the candidate ‘final’ window (pending customer agreement).

2025-06-11 09:02 ET — Simran Kaur: Remaining work: (1) confirm whether we should permanently disable auto-tune for qp-prod-chat or add guardrails (no increases during active benchmark windows), (2) document the measurement methodology + config pin in the Metrics Validation Worksheet, (3) send customer-facing RCA summary for their internal procurement/POC memo. Keeping ticket In Progress until customer confirms acceptance of the rerun window.
resolution: Pending customer confirmation. Mitigation applied: pinned batching config to baseline (max_batch_tokens=8192) and drained one outlier node. Rerun shows p95 back within baseline band. Action items remain to document methodology and decide long-term auto-tune guardrails for the dedicated route.
action_items: Logan Wright: Attach rerun dashboard screenshots + export CSV for 2025-06-07 window to Metrics Validation Worksheet (QuantaPay tab).
Simran Kaur: Draft 1-page customer-facing summary (what changed, why tail increased, what we pinned, and how we’ll prevent drift during benchmarks).
SRE (via Simran): Confirm container digest differences and whether serving image refresh impacted kernel selection; advise if rollback is needed or if config pin is sufficient.
Priyom Das: Align with customer on final measurement window and ensure they approve using the rerun numbers for POC acceptance and any case-study narrative (subject to legal approval).
